questions.stem: A second year student is confused over the similarities between CML and leukemoid reaction. The presence of which of the following favours a diagnosis of leukemoid reaction over chronic myeloid leukemia?

options.label: A
options.text: TLC count of 40,000 cells per microlitre

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C. High LAP score

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male presents with fatigue, easy bruising, and recurrent infections. Physical examination reveals pallor and petechiae. Laboratory tests show a decreased hemoglobin level, decreased platelet count, and an elevated white blood cell count. A bone marrow biopsy reveals increased blast cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)

Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a type of leukemia characterized by the proliferation of immature lymphoid cells (blast cells) in the bone marrow and peripheral blood. It is more common in children but can also occur in adults.

questions.stemHtml: A 38-year-old woman Lalita complains of fatigue and nausea of 2 weeks in duration. Physical examination reveals numerous pustules on the face, as well as splenomegaly and hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin of 6.3 g/dL and platelets of 50,000/mL. A peripheral smear shows malignant cells with findings as shown. The patient develops diffuse purpura, bleeding from the gums, and laboratory features of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). The cytogenetic studies in malignant cells from the patient described in demonstrate a chromosomal translocation. Which of the following genes is most likely found at the translocation site?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D. Retinoic acid receptor

questions.stem: “Smudge cells” in the peripheral smear are characteristic of:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia

questions.stem: A 30-year-old male presents with fever, night sweats, weight loss, and easy bruising. Physical examination reveals hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory tests show a white blood cell count of 150,000/mm³ with a left shift, increased blasts, and the presence of the Philadelphia chromosome (BCR-ABL fusion gene). Bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely type of leukemia?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D. Chronic myeloid leukemia

questions.stem: A 28-year-old male presents with painless enlargement of his cervical lymph nodes, fatigue, and night sweats. Physical examination reveals firm and rubbery lymph nodes. A lymph node biopsy shows Reed-Sternberg cells surrounded by an inflammatory background. Which of the following subtypes of Hodgkin lymphoma is most likely to be associated with this presentation?
questions.solutionHtml:

questions.stem: Patient with bleeding due to platelet function defects has which of the following features?

options.label: A
options.text: Normal platelet count and normal bleeding time

options.label: B
options.text: Normal platelet count and increased bleeding time

options.label: C
options.text: Decreased platelet count and increased bleeding time

options.label: D
options.text: Normal platelet count and decreased bleeding time

questions.answerText: Normal platelet count and increased bleeding time
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Normal platelet count and increased bleeding time

 

The stem of the question clearly mention the fact that there is platelet function defect. It means that the plate­let count is normal with a problem in the functioning of platelets.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a history of prolonged bleeding from a minor injury to his knee. His family reports a history of similar bleeding episodes in male relatives. Laboratory tests reveal a prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and a normal prothrombin time (PT). He has a normal platelet count and unaltered bleeding time. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Hemophilia A

 

Factor VIII activity is significantly decreased. Hemophilia A is a hereditary bleeding disorder caused by a deficiency or dysfunction of coagulation factor VIII (FVIII). It is characterized by a prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and a normal prothrombin time (PT).

questions.stem: A 35-year-old female presents with fatigue, weight loss, fever, and generalized pruritus. Physical examination reveals generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, and splenomegaly. Laboratory tests show elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), elevated serum levels of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and eosinophilia. A lymph node biopsy reveals Reed-Sternberg cells along with eosinophils and plasma cells. Which of the following subtypes of Hodgkin lymphoma is most likely to be associated with this presentation?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B. Mixed cellularity

questions.stem: A 30-year-old female presents with petechiae, ecchymoses, and easy bruising. She reports that she recently had a viral upper respiratory infection. Laboratory tests show a significantly decreased platelet count and normal hemoglobin and white blood cell counts. Peripheral blood smear reveals isolated thrombocytopenia without significant red blood cell or white blood cell abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP)

 

ITP is an autoimmune disorder characterized by isolated thrombocytopenia (low platelet count) and mucocutaneous bleeding manifestations such as petechiae, ecchymoses, and easy bruising. It often follows a viral infection, as in this case. Laboratory tests typically show a normal hemoglobin level and white blood cell count, distinguishing it from other conditions that can cause thrombocytopenia.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old male presents with easy bruising, mucosal bleeding, and petechiae. Laboratory tests reveal thrombocytopenia, and peripheral blood smear shows abnormally large platelets. His father also had a history of bleeding tendency. Bone marrow examination reveals increased megakaryocytes. Genetic testing reveals a mutation in the gene for glycoprotein Ib-IX. Which of the following conditions is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Bernard-Soulier syndrome

 

Bernard-Soulier syndrome is an inherited platelet disorder characterized by a deficiency or dysfunction of the glycoprotein complex Ib-IX, which plays a crucial role in platelet adhesion to von Willebrand factor. This results in abnormally large platelets (giant platelets) and a clinical presentation of easy bruising, mucosal bleeding, and petechiae.

 

The patient's family history of bleeding tendency and the genetic mutation in the gene for glycoprotein Ib-IX are consistent with Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old female with a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and recurrent nosebleeds presents to her physician for evaluation. Laboratory tests reveal a prolonged bleeding time, a prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT), and a normal prothrombin time (PT). Platelet count is within normal limits. The patient has a family history of bleeding disorders. What is the most likely explanation for the laboratory findings in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Von Willebrand disease

 

vWD is characterized by defective or deficient von Willebrand factor (vWF), which plays a crucial role in platelet adhesion and stabilization of factor VIII. While vWD can present with similar laboratory findings, including a prolonged aPTT and decreased factor VIII levels, the presence of family history and the clinical presentation in this patient point more toward hemophilia A.

 

Other Options: 

 

Option B. Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency):

 

  • ↑ aPTT, normal bleeding time
  • No mucosal bleeding typically

 

Option C. Hemophilia B (Factor IX deficiency):

 

  • Same lab pattern as Hemophilia A
  • No mucosal bleeding or menorrhagia

 

Option D. Factor V Leiden mutation:

 

  • Thrombophilic disorder (risk of clotting, not bleeding)
  • Normal bleeding time and aPTT

questions.stem: In an ablated animal, myeloid series cells are injected. Which of following is seen after incubation period?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) RBC

 

When myeloid series cells are injected into an ablated animal (typically one whose bone marrow or hematopoietic system has been destroyed, e.g., by irradiation), the outcome depends on the type of cells injected:

 

  • Myeloid series cells are committed progenitor cells that give rise to:
    • Granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils)
    • Monocytes/macrophages
    • Erythrocytes (RBCs)
    • Platelets

 

After injection and an incubation period, these cells can mature into their respective lineages — most notably, RBCs, because erythroid precursors are part of the myeloid lineage.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Fibroblasts: These are not derived from hematopoietic/myeloid cells — they come from mesenchymal tissue.

 

Option B. T lymphocytes: These arise from lymphoid lineage, not the myeloid series.

 

Option D. Hematopoietic stem cell: This is a pluripotent precursor and would not be present in a myeloid cell injection, as those are already committed.

questions.stem: Which among the following laboratory investigation is best to reveal bleeding in Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Increased FDPs

 

The diagnosis of DIC is based on clinical observation and laboratory measurement of fibrinogen levels, platelets, the PT and PTT, and fibrin degradation products.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the complication of massive blood transfusion?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Metabolic alkalosis

 

Massive transfusion is defined as the need to transfuse from one to two times the patient’s normal blood volume. Most common abnormality is metabolic alkalosis which results from conversion of citrate (present in stored blood) and lactate (accumulated due to hypoperfusion) to bicarbonate.

questions.stem: A voluntary donor underwent apheresis for platelet donation for the first time after which he developed perioral tingling and numbness. This is seen because:

options.label: A
options.text: His platelet count was low for donation

options.label: B
options.text: He underwent apheresis for the first time

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Due to citrate based anticoagulant

 

Apheresis means to separate or to take away. There are now continuous-flow devices in which incoming blood is continuously subjected to a centrifugal force. A standing cell gradient is established. The fraction(s) to be removed are pumped into a bag, and the rest is reinfused continuously.  An increasing proportion of blood components is being collected using automated cell separation
